explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/974: the stronger form with only two distinct runs of n−1 zeros (Erdős's speculation, proved by Tijdeman). The statement assumes two distinct starting points a ≠ b. IsTuranConfiguration encodes the page's description of the resolution: for odd n, the z_i are exactly the n-th roots of unity; for even n, they are the m-th roots of 1 together with the m-th roots of some unimodular c ≠ 1, where m = n/2. Equality of ranges forces z to be injective. Not every such c actually occurs (the zero runs need c^t = −1 for some t), so the conclusion is a necessary condition, slightly weaker than a full characterisation, as is the page's own description. Faithful.
